description.narrative: Congo Energy Solutions Limited (CESL, Nuru, or the Company) is leading a project to develop, build and operate three solar hybrid mini-grid projects in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Each mini-grid will combine solar photovoltaic panels, battery energy storage systems, and diesel generators to provide up to 15MW of generation capacity in Bunia (8MW), Goma (5MW) and Kindu (2MW), the capital cities of DRCs Ituri, North Kivu and Maniema provinces, respectively (the Project). The mini-grids will operate independently (i.e., they will not rely on electric power supply from the main electricity grid). The Project is expected to provide more affordable and reliable electricity to 28,000 households and businesses that currently have expensive, unreliable, unsustainable, or no access to electricity. Potential commercial and industrial off-takers include telecom tower operators, water pumping stations and substations, agri-processing and milling companies, national banks, and water bottling factories. In addition to IFC's own account investment, the Project is expected to be supported by the Finland-IFC Blended Finance for Climate Program, as described in the Blended Finance Section.

The Project is expected to increase access to electricity for residential, commercial and industrial (C&I) and small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) customers, by adding up to 15MW of solar hybrid mini-grids across three provincial capitals. DRC is an FCS country with one of the lowest electrification rates in the world of 19.1%, with only one percent electrification in rural areas. The mini-grids are expected to displace diesel gensets by offering reliable, more affordable and greener electricity supply, resulting in lower GHG emissions. At a market level, the Project is expected to catalyze further development of private mini-grids in the DRC and the SSA region by demonstrating the commercial viability of the business model and helping build investor confidence in DRCs new regulatory and institutional framework. The Project is being developed in parallel to the recently-launched Scaling Mini-Grids (SMG) initiative in the DRC, the first country-level SMG project in Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). As such, it has the potential to generate relevant learnings for future projects in the sector, contributing to its growth.
